verdict: Mostly trustworthy, and close to ready for the team. The Priority cards follow verification.verevon closely: every sampled card uses the corrected exactGap, constraints and approachAdjustment (for example, the resolver location in F-t3-001, the Temporal host decision in F-t3-002, the Do-first MCP scope in F-t3-003, the Z-60/Z-40 reorder in F-t3-005 and the Control-owned contract in F-t3-018). Every Priority card whose reference check came back partial has dropped the refuted reference claim and uses the corrected prevalence. Of the roughly 45 code citations I opened at commit afb83928, all but one support the sentence that cites them. The document should not ship until three factual errors are fixed. First, F-t3-045 says MCP tools are already callable through mcp_call; the code refutes this, and so do the F-t3-003 and F-t3-070 cards. Second, F-t3-022 says the SPA shows cache read tokens per turn, but the Usage frame carries no cache fields, which F-t3-028 itself notes. Third, F-t3-006 points its 'always' rules at F-t3-066 (UI quality gates) instead of the F-t3-032 policy registry. The remaining problems are minor: two wrong denominators (5 of 11, 1 of 11), one citation pointing at the wrong file, one 'every reference' overstatement, a Priority dependency on the demoted F-t3-016 that contradicts the demotion reason, an M4 plan omission, REA tags on SRC records, and named-agent counts that differ between two cards. With the nine proposed patches applied, the cards meet the brief: shared gaps, best source per capability, differentiators, a separate nice-to-have tier and a three-tier sort, all written as an audit that changes nothing.

issues.problem: The card says 'the SPA shows read tokens per turn'. The SPA has a Prompt cache metric, but the server's Usage frame carries no cache_read or cache_write fields, so the metric reads zero. Cache tokens reach only the NATS usage envelope and cost-core. This contradicts the F-t3-028 card, which says correctly that Usage has no cache fields and the metric appears to stay at zero. The F-t3-022 verification repeated the error, but the F-t3-028 verification and the code agree with each other.
